additional_info.subject: ID0385340-DC/Si-D/DE[160355321] - DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 CRM:00315001947
additional_info.body:
Dear Rudi,
Thank you for reaching out to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / N8 160355321
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
cxGiFJ
Problem Description
: DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 → Sessions are aborted
Troubleshooting
:
I've checked the AWS logs and found that we had 7 occurrences in the last 4 weeks:
From our perspective, there has been few errors occuring so <2 occurrences/week.
Me and Integration team have been involved in a topic regarding the eActros 600 PilotState drops, and this can also be a cause for this. The cable might not be in the best condition since this is also a test site for Daimler where they might plug out and plug in much more often than the regular usage.
Can you tell me if this cable was ever replaced before? I believe this SiD is one of the first ever built, so the plug being faulty would not be surprising.
Since this charger is out of warranty we need to align with them on what we should do, if they want to replace the cable or if we should first troubleshoot it and afterwards reach a plan.
From my side, I would need the following:
Photos of the DC contacts of DC2 (something really close up like this:)
As you can see this is an example where we had DC2_CableTempSensor error.
Make sure that all the wires reaching the StateMonitor are properly attached:
You can use the multimeter (before removing the cables and replugging) to measure between the several spots:
XD12:3B/4D to XD12:10D
XD12:3A/4C to XD12:10C
CCS-B IN (J5) CP to CCS-B IN (J5) PP
For future reference, your ticket number is
0385340
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim
Please do not
change
the
subject of this Email when
replying
to it.

I think there is no need from our side to check proactively the Plug.
